proofs.proof_tex:
The completed mixed-support elimination theorem gives finite unions (6) and (12) equal to the full cycle fibers and an exact decision of whether \(\tau_C\) is constant on those unions.  The established cycle-to-SCM lift gives the equalities of target images
\[
\mathcal T_A(p,m)
=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},
\qquad
\mathcal T_B(p)
=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}. \tag{14}
\]
Thus \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\) if and only if the design-A component projections computed by \(\mathscr A(T,m)\) are all singletons with the same value.  The identical argument with the residual-refined union proves the design-B equivalence.  These are observable rank, support, incidence, residual, and cycle tests because every chart choice and every polynomial coefficient is constructed from \(T\), and from \(m\) where it is supplied.

For a real input, the one-copy evaluator is over \(\mathbb K_\zeta\).  A singleton coordinate is either returned by field arithmetic or is algebraic over that field; square-free factorization and Thom signs give the asserted uniquely ordered encoding.  When \(\zeta\) is rational, clearing denominators produces an integer polynomial, and rational root isolation replaces Thom comparison by a rational isolating interval.  If the target image is not a singleton, the component algorithm returns two cycle points with unequal \(\tau_C\); equation (14) and the lift give two legal full SCMs with identical supplied information and unequal \(\tau\).  The interior-support clause proved in the completed elimination theorem and the interior clause of the lift give strictly positive twins exactly on interior nonrigid strata.  This proves every assertion.

Let \(R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\) denote the pair in Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki.  On an observable law satisfying their Conditions 2--3, every compatible member of the present anchor-model fiber satisfies their Condition 1 by the defining response, selection, and proxy factorization.  The cited regular-identification lemma therefore gives
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)
\qquad\text{for every compatible }\vartheta. \tag{15}
\]
The cited lemma includes the positive-observed-probability condition, so every conditioning operation in (15) is defined.  Hence the full target image is the singleton \(\{R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\}\).  By the full-rigidity theorem, \(\mathscr A\) declares this fiber rigid and returns its unique value, which by (15) is precisely the published Appendix value.

For any other nonempty observable fiber, including a rank-one cell, coincident endpoint, inactive coefficient row, or forced-zero face, the structural equality (6) assigns every design-A cycle point to a local mode and support chart.  In design B, (12) additionally assigns every compatible point to either the zero-residual or active proportional state at each response type and imposes all forest scales, cycle products, and relevance.  Thus these singular and boundary laws are in the domain of the same compiler, without invoking the regular inversions in (15).  The full-rigidity theorem then returns exactly one of two exhaustive alternatives: all one-copy component projections agree at an exact target value, or two component samples lift to legal target-changing SCMs.  This proves the universal boundary-coverage clause as well as regular-domain agreement.

Let \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\) satisfy the stated no-selection overlap and \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_\vartheta)\).  The cited Kawakami identification lemma applies under exactly the recursive factorization, invertibility, separation, and exclusion conditions included in \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}\); its simultaneous equations identify \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\).

In the comparator order \((00,01,10,11)\), response consistency implies that \(X=1,Y=1\) admits precisely types \(01\) and \(11\), while \(X=0,Y=0\) admits precisely types \(00\) and \(01\).  Selected-table positivity and \(S=1\) almost surely make both conditioning events positive.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{PN}(\vartheta)
=\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}}
{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,4}},
\qquad
\operatorname{PS}(\vartheta)
=\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}
{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,1}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}, \tag{16}
\]
which is \(\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K})\).  If \(\mathcal T_B(p)\) is a singleton, it contains \(\tau(\vartheta)\) by definition; hence (16) is its unique value.  The full-rigidity theorem makes the atlas value equal to that unique element.  The cited Kawakami lemma also supplies the stated identified scope: four joint binary potential-outcome-type probabilities and the treatment-conditional weights recovered in its proof.

It remains to verify the strict scope-separation datum.  By the already established experimental-proxy reduction and boundary-separation theorem,
\[
\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing,
\qquad
\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}. \tag{17}
\]
For either \(x\), each row of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is
\[
(1,b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_1),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_2),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_3)).
\]
Because \(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\) is a probability vector on the three-point alphabet,
\[
1=b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_1)+b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_2)+b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_3)
\]
row by row.  Hence the first column of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is the sum of its last three columns, so its determinant is zero for \(x=0,1\).  The datum therefore violates the named invertibility condition in Kawakami's Theorem 1(i), while (17) and the full atlas give a legal selected rigid law.  This establishes a one-law strict scope separation and makes no subsumption claim.

Put \(N_0=k\ell+k+\ell\).  Before support refinement, a design-A structural chart uses at most \(4\ell+8k\) endpoint and incident-coefficient coordinates; one coefficient row per edge may be replaced by \(v_e-a_{ei}\).  Design B adds at most \(k-1\) projective coordinates, four cell margins, four response weights or their reconstructed equivalents, and four component scales.  Thus the number \(N\) of scalar variables is at most \(C_0N_0\).  The table equations contribute at most \(4k\ell\) bilinear equations.  Simplex, mode, incidence, support, residual-minor, forest, normalization, and relevance conditions contribute at most \(C_0N_0\) further polynomial sign conditions.  By retaining the original endpoint and coefficient variables and clearing only declared positive or signed pivots, all degrees are bounded by a universal constant \(d_0\) (one may take a larger constant to cover the four-link cycle product).

For each of four edges there are two rank-two orientations or the rank-one choices \({\rm L},{\rm R},{\rm D}\) and the \(3^k\) faces of \({\rm E}\).  Endpoint-coordinate, coefficient-coordinate, incidence-pivot, four residual-state, forest-root, cycle-orientation, and relevance-sign refinements add at most \(3^{C_1N_0}\) choices.  Hence the number of labeled structural charts is at most
\[
M_{k,\ell}\le 2^{C_2N_0}. \tag{18}
\]
Every choice is made by finitely many arithmetic and order tests over \(\mathbb K_\zeta\), and the structural equality in the mixed-support theorem shows that discarding an empty chart loses no fiber point.

Apply the cited one-copy real-algebraic algorithm to each chart graph.  With
\(s\le C_3N_0\), \(d\le d_0\), and \(N\le C_0N_0\), its conservative complexity and output-degree envelope is
\[
(sd)^{2^{O(N)}}\le 2^{2^{C_4N_0}}. \tag{19}
\]
Enlarging a universal constant \(C\) and defining
\[
B_{k,\ell}=2^{2^{C(k\ell+k+\ell)}}
\]
makes (18), every component count, and every algebraic degree no larger than \(B_{k,\ell}\).  This proves termination and the displayed bound over an arbitrary ordered input field.

Now suppose every input coordinate is rational with numerator and denominator bit length at most \(L\).  Forming \(r\), \(v\), normalized columns, minors, and cleared chart equations increases coefficient bit length to at most \(C_5N_0(L+1)^{C_5}\).  The integer-input clause of the cited algorithm and (19), after another enlargement of \(C\), bounds every output coefficient and rational isolating endpoint by
\[
B_{k,\ell}(L+1)^C. \tag{20}
\]
Square-free factorization does not increase the degree, and exact real-root isolation supplies rational endpoints.  Therefore a Turing implementation halts with the claimed certificate.  The only real-algebraic calls were the component and target projection calls on the one-copy graphs after the finite response-cycle modes had been enumerated; no two-copy unequal-target classifier occurs.

Let \(K\) be a compact subset of \(\mathfrak R_\varepsilon\).  Independent multinomial sampling, proportional margin-sample scaling when needed, and the cited finite-multinomial theorem give, uniformly over \(K\),
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_\zeta),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_\zeta. \tag{21}
\]
For every incident chart \(\chi\), \(d_\chi(\zeta)=0\).  Since distance to a closed set is one-Lipschitz,
\[
d_\chi(\widehat\zeta_n)
\le\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2
=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(t_n),
\qquad t_n=n^{-1/4}. \tag{22}
\]
Continuity of the finitely many normalized slacks and
\(\eta_\chi(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\) make the slack test exceed
\(\varepsilon/2\) with probability tending to one.  Conversely, the
\(\varepsilon\)-distance from every incompatible chart closure and the
one-Lipschitz property imply
\[
d_\chi(\widehat\zeta_n)\ge
\varepsilon-\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2>t_n
\]
with probability tending to one for every incompatible chart.  Finiteness of the completed atlas, its disjoint sign refinement, and compactness make these statements uniform.  A qualifying chart whose closure meets the true law is incident there; the separation clause excludes every qualifying nonincident incompatible chart.  Thus the lexicographic rule chooses an incident first-order-compatible rigid chart with probability tending to one.  All eligible incident charts have the common target and Jacobian required in \(\mathfrak R_\varepsilon\).  In particular the selected value is centered at the unique causal target certified by the full-rigidity theorem.

On the selected chart, the twice continuously differentiable extension and Taylor's theorem give
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
=J_\chi(\zeta)\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+o_P(1), \tag{23}
\]
uniformly over \(K\); the common-value and common-Jacobian condition makes (23) independent of the lexicographic choice.  Equations (21)--(23), the delta method, and Slutsky's theorem yield
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)\Rightarrow
N(0,V_\tau),
\qquad
V_\tau=J_\chi(\zeta)\Omega_\zeta J_\chi(\zeta)^{\top}. \tag{24}
\]
Continuity of \(J_\chi\) and (21) also gives
\[
\widehat V_n
=J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)
\widehat\Omega_n
J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)^{\top}
\xrightarrow{P}V_\tau. \tag{25}
\]
The lower bound \(\lambda_{\min}(V_\tau)\ge\varepsilon\) and (25) imply that the raw sandwich matrix is positive definite with probability tending to one, hence \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with that probability.  The quadratic form in (24)--(25) converges to \(\chi^2_2\); every fixed scalar contrast with positive limiting variance has its corresponding standard-normal limit.  Consequently the elliptical branch of \(W_n\), and the usual scalar Wald intervals, have limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).

If no chart is certified, the definitions directly give
\(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(F_\bot=(0,0)\), \(J_\bot=0\),
\(\widehat\tau_n=(0,0)\), \(\widehat V_n=I_2\), and
\(W_n=[0,1]^2\).  None of (23)--(25) was asserted on this fallback event outside the separated regime, which proves the final clause.

Let \(q_0\) denote the true observable law, including the independent margin law in design A when it is sampled, and put \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\).  By the definition of the corresponding full fiber and target set,
\[
t_0\in\mathcal T(q_0). \tag{26}
\]
Each multinomial cell count is marginally binomial.  A two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval is obtained by inverting its two exact binomial tail tests, so its two noncoverage tails are bounded by their allocated probabilities.  Bonferroni's inequality over all selected-table and independent-margin cells therefore gives
\[
P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}\le\beta_n. \tag{27}
\]
This uses neither a rank condition nor identification.

For a fixed compatible pair \((q,t)\), define the random upper-tail value
\[
G_{q,t}=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)
\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\mid\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}.
\]
The proved discrete-tail lemma, applied to the replicate statistic, gives
\[
P_q(G_{q,t}\le u)\le u\qquad(0\le u\le1). \tag{28}
\]
On the event \(q_0\in C_n\), equations (26) and the supremum in the definition of \(\operatorname{pv}_n\) imply
\[
\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)
\ge\min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\}. \tag{29}
\]
Since \(\beta_n\le\alpha/2\), exclusion of \(t_0\) from \(K_n\) and (27)--(29) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
&\le P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}
+P_{q_0}\{G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n\}\\
&\le\beta_n+(\alpha-\beta_n)=\alpha.
\end{aligned} \tag{30}
\]
This proves finite-sample coverage.  The argument is pointwise at every sample size and contains no continuity constant; applying it to each member of any triangular array proves the same bound along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\), including point-to-set transitions.

It remains to compare the regular branches.  Fix a compact subset of \(\mathfrak R_\varepsilon\).  The full structural atlas and its separation conditions give a neighborhood in which every compatible target graph is one of finitely many incident first-order-compatible graphs
\(t=F_\chi(q)\), while incompatible chart closures remain separated.  The separated-Wald theorem makes the selector use their common value and Jacobian with probability tending to one.  The cited smooth multinomial likelihood theorem, applied uniformly to these finitely many twice continuously differentiable graphs, gives for
\(\|t-\tau\|=O(n^{-1/2})\)
\[
\Delta_n(t)
=n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}
\widehat V_n^{-1}(t-\widehat\tau_n)+o_P(1), \tag{31}
\]
uniformly in \(t\) and in the true law on the compact set.  Equality of the incident Jacobians makes the leading quadratic in (31) the same for every glued chart; the positive eigenvalue bound makes it coercive.

The preliminary region satisfies \(\sup_{q\in C_n}\|q-q_0\|=o_P(1)\): exact binomial inversion with \(\beta_n\ge0\) and \(\beta_n\asymp n^{-2}\) gives widths of order at most \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) on an interior compact set.  The uniform profile-Wilks part of the cited theorem and \(\beta_n\to0\) therefore imply that the supremum replicate tail in \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t)\) has the \(\chi^2_2\) upper tail, uniformly on the root-\(n\) boundary.  Hence (31) gives
\[
K_n=
\left\{t\in[0,1]^2:
n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}\widehat V_n^{-1}
(t-\widehat\tau_n)le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}+o_P(1)
\right\} \tag{32}
\]
in root-\(n\) Hausdorff scale.  Positive definiteness bounded away from zero converts the \(o_P(1)\) perturbation of the quadratic boundary into an \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) Euclidean perturbation.  Comparing (32) with the definition of the elliptical branch of \(W_n\) proves
\[
\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0.
\]
At a non-singleton target set or outside the separated smooth conditions, only (30) was used.  Thus no shrinking-diameter assertion is made there.

theorem.statement: For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), the compiler \(\mathscr A\) can be completed as follows.  Its design-A charts have coordinates \((b,a)\) and form an exhaustive finite disjoint structural atlas for every nonempty \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) by combining the two oriented rank-two segment modes with the four rank-one modes \({\rm L},{\rm R},{\rm E},{\rm D}\), all split-coordinate faces of \({\rm E}\), all coefficient and endpoint support faces, and all endpoint-incidence pivot signs, while using one shared variable \(b_i\) at the two cells incident to response type \(i\).  For \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) it adjoins \(\rho>0\), the zero-residual or lexicographically pivoted active negative-proportional state at every response type, residual-forest propagation, the active four-cycle product, positive component scales with normalization, and the relevance inequality.  These unions equal \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) and \(\mathcal C_B(T)\), respectively, including simultaneous rank-one cells, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, and forced-zero faces.  On each resulting one-copy chart, an exact component/projection algorithm over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) computes the graph of \(\tau_C\), decides constancy on every real component, and compares all component values.  It returns either the common exact value, as a rational expression when it lies in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) and otherwise by a square-free polynomial and Thom signs, or two legal target-changing full-SCM lifts.  The latter lifts may lie on boundary faces, and they are strictly positive when the nonrigid chart is an interior support chart.  No two-copy unequal-target quantifier-elimination predicate is used in constructing or classifying the structural atlas.
theorem.proof_tex:
Write \(k=|\mathcal Z|\), \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), and fix once and for all an order of cells, response types, proxy coordinates, and instrument coordinates.  Selected-table positivity implies
\[
r_e>0,\qquad v_e(z)>0,
\qquad c_{ez}:=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}^{\circ}.
\tag{2}
\]
Every matrix in a two-column nonnegative factorization has rank at most two.  Since (2) rules out rank zero, nonemptiness of either cycle fiber implies
\(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)\in\{1,2\}\) for every cell.  The ranks and all equalities among the observed normalized columns are determined by minors with coefficients in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).

\emph{Rank-two local charts.}
Suppose \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=2\).  In any factorization, division by \(v_e(z)>0\) gives
\[
c_{ez}=q_{ez}b_i+(1-q_{ez})b_j,
\qquad q_{ez}:=a_{ei}(z)/v_e(z)\in[0,1]. \tag{3}
\]
Rank two forces \(b_i\ne b_j\), and (3) says that all observed column points lie in the closed segment with those endpoints.  Conversely, if two distinct probability vectors on the observed affine line bracket every \(c_{ez}\), equation (3) has unique coefficients in \([0,1]\), and multiplying by \(v_e(z)\) gives the unique nonnegative cell coefficients.

Choose the lexicographically first proxy coordinate \(h_e\) which is nonconstant on the observed column points.  It exists because the normalized columns span an affine line.  In the orientation \(b_i(h_e)<b_j(h_e)\), the exact chart conditions and coefficient formula are
\[
b_i(h_e)\le\min_z c_{ez}(h_e),\qquad
b_j(h_e)\ge\max_z c_{ez}(h_e),
\qquad
q_{ez}=\frac{b_j(h_e)-c_{ez}(h_e)}{b_j(h_e)-b_i(h_e)}. \tag{4}
\]
The reverse orientation interchanges the inequalities.  The denominator in (4) has a declared strict sign.  Thus clearing it preserves every inequality and produces polynomial chart conditions over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The two orientations are disjoint and exhaustive.  Splitting each \(q_{ez}\) into \(0\), \((0,1)\), or \(1\) records every endpoint equality and forced coefficient zero.  This is the local segment construction underlying the already established rank-two orientation theorem, now retained edge by edge.

\emph{Rank-one local charts.}
If \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=1\), the rank-one normal-form lemma applies because of (2).  Hence the cell is in exactly one of \({\rm L},{\rm R},{\rm E},{\rm D}\).  In particular, an inactive row leaves its unused endpoint as a genuine arbitrary point of \(\Delta_{\mathcal W}\); it is not silently placed in the span of the observed tables.  In mode \({\rm E}\), every vector \(s_e\) is retained, and its \(3^k\) coordinate faces exhaust the box \(0\le s_e\le v_e\).  In \({\rm D}\), \(q_e\in(0,1)\) remains a chart variable.  Thus no proportional instrument information carried by an equal-endpoint split is discarded.

\emph{Global design-A union.}
Take the Cartesian product of the local mode choices over the four response-cycle edges, but use one global variable \(b_i\), not separate copies, for the two occurrences of response type \(i\).  Add the simplex equations
\[
b_i(w)\ge0,qquad \sum_wb_i(w)=1, \tag{5}
\]
and refine by the signs of the following finite family: every \(b_i(w)\); every \(a_{ei}(z)\) and \(v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z)\); every coordinate of \(b_i-b_j\) and \(b_i-c_e\) appearing in a rank-one mode; the pivot minors comparing an endpoint displacement with each incident observed-line direction; and every pivot or denominator used in (4).  A line direction uses its lexicographically first nonzero coordinate, so incidence requires only one proportionality equation per remaining coordinate.  Zero is separated from each of the two strict signs, and any other nonzero vector likewise uses its lexicographically first nonzero coordinate as pivot.  Consequently these refinements are finite and disjoint, and explicitly include coincident lines, coincident endpoints, endpoint incidences, inactive vertices, and every support face.

Let the resulting semialgebraic sets be \(X^A_{\gamma}(T)\).  If
\((b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\), its observable ranks choose a rank at every edge; (3)--(4) choose exactly one rank-two orientation and coefficient face; the rank-one lemma chooses exactly one rank-one mode and split face; and the actual signs choose exactly one global refinement.  Because the same actual \(b_i\) is used at both incident cells, the point lies in one \(X^A_\gamma(T)\).  This proves
\[
\mathcal C_A(T)\subseteq\bigcup_\gamma X^A_\gamma(T). \tag{6}
\]
Conversely, (3)--(5) and the four rank-one formulas give normalized nonnegative endpoints and coefficients, the equality
\(a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e\), and
\(T_e=b_ia_{ei}^{\top}+b_ja_{ej}^{\top}\) on every edge.  Hence every chart point is in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\), proving the reverse inclusion in (6).  This is an equality of the full nonnegative fiber, not merely of a dense or generic subset.

\emph{Global design-B union.}
Fix a baseline \(z_0\) and adjoin \(\rho_{z_0}=1\), \(\rho_z>0\).  At response type \(i\), order its incident cells as \((e_i,f_i)\).  There are exactly two feasible residual states.  The zero state is
\[
D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i}(\rho)=D^{\mathrm{res}}_{f_i i}(\rho)=0. \tag{7}
\]
For an active state, choose the lexicographically first coordinate \(h\ne z_0\) at which
\(D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i,h}\ne0\), choose its sign, and impose
\[
\begin{gathered}
D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i,h}D^{\mathrm{res}}_{f_i i,h}<0,\\
D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i,u}D^{\mathrm{res}}_{f_i i,h}
-D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i,h}D^{\mathrm{res}}_{f_i i,u}=0
\quad(u\ne z_0),\\
R_i:=-\frac{D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i,h}}
{D^{\mathrm{res}}_{f_i i,h}}>0,\qquad m_{f_i}=R_im_{e_i}.
\end{gathered} \tag{8}
\]
The preceding residual coordinates are set to zero.  Thus the pivot choices in (8) are finite, disjoint, and say exactly that the two residuals are nonzero and negatively proportional.  A state with exactly one zero residual is excluded.

The active links form a subgraph of the four-cycle on the cell vertices.  Every proper subgraph is a forest.  In each forest component choose its least cell as root, multiply the ratios \(R_i\) along the unique root-to-cell path, and write
\[
m_e=\lambda_C R_e,qquad \lambda_C>0,qquad
\sum_C\lambda_C\sum_{e\in C}R_e=1. \tag{9}
\]
Here \(R_e=1\) at a root.  If all four links are active, use a spanning tree in (9) and impose that the product of the four directed ratios around the cycle is one.  Denominators have declared nonzero signs, so (8)--(9) are equivalently finite polynomial sign conditions.  Finally set
\[
g(z)=\frac{\rho_z}{\sum_u\rho_u},qquad
q^X_z=\sum_{e:e_X=1}m_e\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_e}a_{ei}(z), \tag{10}
\]
and refine the relevance disjunction by the lexicographically first pair and sign for which
\[
q^X_z\rho_{z'}-q^X_{z'}\rho_z\ne0. \tag{11}
\]
The established IV residual-forest theorem proves both directions: every point of \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) has exactly one state (7) or (8) at every response type, its positive margins have representation (9), every active cycle obeys the product constraint, and relevance gives (11); conversely (7)--(11) reconstruct positive margins satisfying all shared-\(Z\) equations, a normalized positive \(g\), response weights \(\pi\), and relevance.  Combining this result with (6) therefore gives
\[
\mathcal C_B(T)=\bigcup_\delta X^B_\delta(T), \tag{12}
\]
where the union is over finitely many explicit structural choices.  Equations (7) and (9) retain zero-residual vertices and free component scales, so (12) also covers every simultaneous inactive-row and hidden-split pattern.

\emph{One-copy component evaluation and gluing.}
For either design and every nonempty chart \(X_\gamma\), form the one-copy graph
\[
G_\gamma=
\{(x,t):x\in X_\gamma,\ t_1=\textstyle\sum_z a_{11,2}(z),\
t_2=\textstyle\sum_z a_{00,2}(z)\}. \tag{13}
\]
All variables in (13) occur once.  The coefficients belong to \(\mathbb K_\zeta\), and the target equations are linear.  Apply the cited effective semialgebraic component and projection theorem to compute a roadmap and a sample point for every semialgebraically connected component \(C\) of \(X_\gamma\), then compute the target projection of the restricted graph \(G_\gamma|_C\).  Sign-invariant decomposition decides whether each of its two coordinate projections is a singleton.  If a projection is not a singleton, its decomposition contains either two distinct zero-dimensional cells or a positive-dimensional cell; in either case the sampling-and-lifting procedure returns two points of \(C\) with different target values.  If both projections are singletons, their real-univariate representations give the constant pair on \(C\).  Thom signs compare these constants across all components and all charts.

By (6) and (12), constancy on every component together with equality of the component constants is necessary and sufficient for constancy of \(\tau_C\) on the entire cycle fiber.  A singleton semialgebraic set defined over \(\mathbb K_\zeta\) consists of elements algebraic over that field.  The cited algorithm therefore returns an element of \(\mathbb K_\zeta\) as an arithmetic expression when elimination is linear, and otherwise a square-free polynomial together with Thom signs selecting the uniquely ordered real root.  If target constancy fails, the two sampled one-copy chart points either come from one nonconstant projection or from two components with unequal constants.  The established cycle-to-SCM lift maps them to two legal full SCMs with the same observables and, in design A, the same supplied margins, while preserving \(\tau=\tau_C\).  On an interior support chart all endpoint, coefficient, margin, instrument, selection, and assignment inequalities required by the lift are strict; choosing the samples in that chart and applying the interior clause of the lift gives strictly positive twins.  Boundary comparisons require, and return, only legal nonnegative twins.

The construction before (13) uses only the enumerated response-cycle modes, shared endpoints, residual states, forest ratios, and relevance.  The real-algebraic routine is applied separately to the one-copy graph of each already exhaustive chart.  At no point is a formula with two factorization copies and an unequal-target predicate used.  This proves the asserted completion of \(\mathscr A\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(e\in\mathcal E\) have \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\), and suppose that \(T_e\) has rank one.  Put \(c_e=T_e(\cdot,z)/v_e(z)\), which is independent of \(z\).  Every factorization of this cell in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) belongs to exactly one of the following disjoint modes (with the coincident case assigned to mode \({\rm E}\)):
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
({\rm L})&a_{ei}\equiv0,\quad b_j=c_e,\quad b_i\ne c_e;\\
({\rm R})&a_{ej}\equiv0,\quad b_i=c_e,\quad b_j\ne c_e;\\
({\rm E})&b_i=b_j=c_e,\quad a_{ei}(z)=s_e(z),\quad
             a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-s_e(z),\quad0\le s_e(z)\le v_e(z);\\
({\rm D})&b_i\ne b_j,\quad c_e=q_e b_i+(1-q_e)b_j,\quad
             a_{ei}(z)=q_ev_e(z),\quad a_{ej}(z)=(1-q_e)v_e(z),
             \quad0<q_e<1.
\end{array}
\]
Conversely, every parameter tuple in one of these modes is a valid rank-one cell factorization.  Mode \({\rm E}\) is the disjoint union of the \(3^{|\mathcal Z|}\) split-coordinate faces obtained by declaring, for each \(z\), exactly one of \(s_e(z)=0\), \(0<s_e(z)<v_e(z)\), and \(s_e(z)=v_e(z)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Selected-table positivity gives \(T_e(w,z)>0\) and therefore
\[
v_e(z)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}T_e(w,z)>0
\qquad(z\in\mathcal Z).
\]
Because \(T_e\) is nonzero and has rank one, all of its columns are positive multiples of one positive probability vector.  Normalization by their positive sums consequently gives a single vector \(c_e\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}^{\circ}\) such that
\[
T_e(\cdot,z)=v_e(z)c_e
\qquad(z\in\mathcal Z).
\]
For a cell factorization define the well-typed number
\[
q_z=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1],
\]
where the interval assertion follows from nonnegativity and
\(a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)\).  Dividing
\(T_e(\cdot,z)=b_i a_{ei}(z)+b_j a_{ej}(z)\) by \(v_e(z)>0\) yields
\[
c_e=q_zb_i+(1-q_z)b_j. \tag{1}
\]
If \(b_i=b_j\), equation (1) and normalization give
\(b_i=b_j=c_e\), while the only remaining restriction is
\(0\le a_{ei}(z)\le v_e(z)\).  This is exactly mode \({\rm E}\), with
\(s_e(z)=a_{ei}(z)\).

Suppose instead that \(b_i\ne b_j\).  Subtracting (1) at two coordinates
\(z,z'\) gives
\[
(q_z-q_{z'})(b_i-b_j)=0.
\]
Since the vector \(b_i-b_j\) is nonzero, \(q_z=q_{z'}\) for every pair;
write the common value as \(q_e\).  If \(q_e=0\), then
\(a_{ei}\equiv0\), \(a_{ej}=v_e\), and (1) gives \(b_j=c_e\).  The
assumed endpoint inequality also gives \(b_i\ne c_e\), so this is
\({\rm L}\).  The case \(q_e=1\) is symmetrically \({\rm R}\).  If
\(0<q_e<1\), equation (1) and the displayed coefficient identities give
\({\rm D}\).  The alternatives are mutually exclusive by the endpoint
equality and the three disjoint possibilities for \(q_e\).  Substitution
into the factorization equation proves the converse in every case.  Finally,
since \(v_e(z)>0\), the three stated alternatives for each coordinate of
\(s_e\) are disjoint and exhaustive; their Cartesian product has
\(3^{|\mathcal Z|}\) members.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(K\) be an ordered subfield of \(\mathbb R\), and let a semialgebraic set in \(N\) variables be described by a Boolean combination of sign conditions on \(s\) polynomials of degree at most \(d\) over \(K\).  Effective sign determination, quantifier elimination, and roadmap/sample-point algorithms compute projections, decide emptiness and signs, and return a real-univariate representation meeting every semialgebraically connected component.  The outputs may be encoded by square-free polynomials and Thom signs over \(K\).  A conservative common bound for the arithmetic work, the number and degree of output polynomials, and, for integer input coefficients of bit length \(H\), the output coefficient and isolating-endpoint bit lengths, is
\[
(sd)^{2^{O(N)}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
(H+1)(sd)^{2^{O(N)}},
\]
respectively.

source.locator: Algorithms 13.1--13.2, Theorem 14.16, and the roadmap and connected-component algorithms in Chapters 15--16

attestation.note: The cited source is Basu, Pollack, and Roy, Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry, second edition; the displayed bound is a deliberately looser common doubly-exponential envelope for its exact sampling, quantifier-elimination, sign, and roadmap outputs.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under independent multinomial sampling from \(p\), with an independent margin sample from \(m\) satisfying \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\) when present, and with \((p,m)\) in a compact subset of the relevant interior simplices,
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_\zeta),
\qquad \widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_\zeta
\]
uniformly.  Continuously differentiable maps satisfy the delta method.  For a twice continuously differentiable, locally full-rank restriction of codimension \(q\), the multinomial profile likelihood-ratio statistic has the uniform local quadratic expansion and the \(\chi^2_q\) limit; the corresponding likelihood and Wald confidence boundaries differ by \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) in Hausdorff distance when the information and restriction covariance eigenvalues are bounded away from zero.

attestation.note: The statement records the finite-dimensional multinomial specialization of the cited central-limit, delta, local asymptotic normality, and likelihood-ratio results; compact-uniformity follows from the displayed interior and eigenvalue separations.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(R\) be any real-valued statistic with an arbitrary, possibly discrete, distribution, let \(R'\) be an independent copy, and define \(G(R)=P(R'\ge R)\).  Then
\[
P\{G(R)\le u\}\le u
\qquad(0\le u\le1).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The case \(u=1\) is immediate.  For \(0\le u<1\), let \(H(x)=P(R\ge x)\), a nonincreasing tail function.  If the set \(A_u=\{x:H(x)\le u\}\) is empty, the result is immediate.  Otherwise \(H(x)\to1\) as \(x\to-\infty\), so \(x_u=\inf A_u\) is finite.  The event \(H(R)\le u\) is contained in \(\{R\ge x_u\}\); if the infimum is not attained, it is contained in \(\{R>x_u\}\).  In the attained case,
\[
P\{H(R)\le u\}\le P(R\ge x_u)=H(x_u)\le u.
\]
In the nonattained case choose \(x_j\downarrow x_u\) with \(x_j\in A_u\).  Then
\[
P(R>x_u)=\lim_{j\to\infty}P(R\ge x_j)le u
\]
by continuity from below.  Since conditioning on \(R\) gives
\(P(R'\ge R\mid R)=H(R)=G(R)\), the displayed inequality is the claim.

proposed.statement: For every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\) in the no-selection overlap satisfying \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\), the simultaneous equations in the proof of Kawakami (2021), Theorem 1 on pages 12135--12137 identify \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\). If \(\mathcal T_B(p)\) is a singleton, its atlas value agrees with \(\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K})\). Kawakami's identified scope is the four joint probabilities of binary potential-outcome types, together with their treatment-conditional weights used for PN and PS, under Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii). For the single explicit selected boundary datum \((p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\), \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\), but \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is singular for each \(x\): because \(\mathcal W=\{w_1,w_2,w_3\}\), its first column is the sum of its last three columns. Thus this legal selected response-cycle law violates the named invertibility assumption in Kawakami's Theorem 1(i) while remaining classified by the atlas; this is a strict scope separation, not a subsumption claim.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Add the defining IV-fiber and response-consistency premises used in the treatment-conditional response-type calculation.

proposed.statement: For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the finite structural chart enumeration of \(\mathscr A\) terminates using arithmetic and order tests over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). There is an explicit computable constant \(B_{k,\ell}\le 2^{2^{C(k\ell+k+\ell)}}\), for a universal constant \(C\), bounding the number of labeled charts and the algebraic degree over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). If every coordinate of \(\zeta\) is an explicitly encoded rational whose numerator and denominator have binary length at most \(L\), a Turing implementation terminates; after clearing denominators, every algebraic target certificate uses a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(B_{k,\ell}\) and rational isolating endpoints, and every coefficient and endpoint has bit length at most \(B_{k,\ell}(L+1)^C\). The classification is obtained from the structural charts in \(\mathscr A\), not by reporting generic two-copy quantifier elimination.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the published exact real-algebraic sampling and complexity theorem used after the structural chart enumeration.

proposed.statement: Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), under independent multinomial sampling and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\) when margins are estimated, the deterministic selector \(\widehat\chi_n\) chooses an incident first-order-compatible rigid chart and \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with probability tending to one. On these certified separated rigid charts, \(\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)\Rightarrow N(0,V_{\tau})\), and \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}\). Because \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), scalar contrasts and the elliptical branch of \(W_n\) have asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). If no chart is certified, the total procedure returns \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(\widehat\tau_n=(0,0)\), \(\widehat V_n=I_2\), and \(W_n=[0,1]^2\), with no covariance-consistency or Wald-coverage assertion for that fallback branch.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the finite-multinomial central-limit and smooth likelihood substrate used by the chartwise delta-method proof.

proposed.statement: For the Clopper--Pearson preliminary region \(C_n\), profile discrepancy \(\Delta_n\), and Berger--Boos calibration in \(\operatorname{pv}_n\), \(P_{\vartheta}\{\tau(\vartheta)\in K_n\}\ge 1-\alpha\) at every sample size for every \(\vartheta\) in either design. The bound holds along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\), including point-to-set transitions. Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0\); equivalently, the local profile boundary and the Wald ellipse have the same first-order quadratic expansion and \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\) calibration. At any law with a non-singleton identified set or without the separated-chart conditions, the theorem asserts coverage only and makes no claim that \(\operatorname{diam}(K_n)\) shrinks.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the proved discrete-tail calibration lemma and the smooth multinomial profile theorem used by the two coverage branches.

prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, the response-cycle compiler now gives a boundary-complete necessary-and-sufficient test for rigidity of the causal pair \(\tau=(\mathrm{PN},\mathrm{PS})\). Its exhaustive local modes retain inactive endpoints and equal-endpoint split vectors, while the IV design adds zero or active residual states, forest scales, the active-cycle product, and relevance. A one-copy real-algebraic component evaluator then returns a common exact target or two legal same-observable full SCMs; strict-positive twins are required only on interior support charts. The resulting atlas agrees with the published regular proxy formulas, terminates with fixed-alphabet exact bounds, supports Wald inference on separated smooth rigid strata, and supports exact confidence-fiber coverage at rank and support transitions. The GEUVADIS application is specified as a known-selection IV audit, but its numerical classification still requires the released cell table and binarization inputs.

project_justification.gap: Published selected-proxy and IV-plus-proxy formulas identify response-type targets under regular invertibility and separation, but do not decide causal-target constancy across simultaneous rank loss, inactive latent rows, coincident endpoints, forced coefficient zeros, or unknown population margins coupled by response-level shared-instrument equations.
project_justification.niche: The four binary response types form a labeled causal cycle. Factorization uniqueness is stronger than necessary: \(\tau_C\) can be constant while nuisance endpoints or equal-endpoint split vectors move. The relevant object is therefore the target image of the full nonnegative SCM fiber, stratified by observable rank, support, incidence, residual, and cycle data.
project_justification.fill: The exhaustive edge-state atlas proves equality between its finite structural union and each normalized cycle fiber. One-copy component projection decides within- and cross-component target agreement over the ordered input field, and the established cycle-to-SCM lift converts every disagreement into legal observationally equivalent causal models. Exact output bounds and separated or transition-robust inference complete the operational map.

sampling_model.overlap: All population selected-table cells are positive, so every \(v_e(z)\) used for normalization is positive and every compatible population cell margin is positive. Wald inference additionally requires an incident rigid chart with slack at least \(\varepsilon\), twice continuously differentiable continuation, separation from incompatible chart closures, and \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\). Boundary and transition laws remain covered by confidence-fiber inversion without a rank-stability premise.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Reduced multinomial coordinates use empirical frequencies and the block-diagonal plug-in covariance. The deterministic chart rule reports a Wald ellipse only after a separated rigid chart and positive-definite sandwich are certified; otherwise it reports the full-square fallback. Transition inference uses exact multinomial replicate tails, a Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson preliminary region, and Berger--Boos calibration over the complete causal target fiber.

prose_updates.related_work: Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026), Theorem 1 and Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33), supply the selected four-response-type model and regular PN/PS inversions; the atlas proof establishes agreement there and extends the decision domain to every nonnegative rank/support face. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023) identify all four response-type probabilities in a randomized no-selection proxy experiment, and the established experimental reduction verifies the exact label-converted overlap plus a selected assignment-boundary law. Kawakami (2021), Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii), identify binary potential-outcome types under regular IV-plus-proxy matrix conditions; the overlap theorem derives the same PN/PS transformation and separately exhibits a selected rigid law with singular \(A_x^{\mathrm K}\), a scope separation rather than a subsumption claim. NMF rigidity and partial-identifiability results concern factor recovery, whereas this theorem classifies a causal target on a labeled shared-endpoint cycle. Basu, Pollack, and Roy supply only the classical one-copy component, projection, sampling, and complexity substrate used after the causal structural modes have been proved exhaustive.
prose_updates.interpretation: Rigidity means that every full SCM compatible with the causal graph, selected law, and supplied information has the same PN/PS pair; it is not defined by an inverse formula or by uniqueness of the latent proxy factorization. A rigid certificate is therefore an identifying map from observables to the singleton target image. A nonrigid certificate is constructive partial identification: two legal full SCMs agree on all supplied observables and margins but disagree on the causal target.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact structural theorem is finite-alphabet and its real-algebraic component evaluator has a conservative doubly-exponential worst-case envelope; no claim of numerical efficiency is made. Arbitrary real inputs are handled relative to their ordered coefficient field, while integer-polynomial bit bounds require explicitly rational encodings. Wald conclusions exclude repeated-root, incompatible-chart, and singular-covariance regimes. Exact confidence coverage remains valid there, but confidence fibers need not shrink at genuinely nonidentified laws. The GEUVADIS numerical audit is not completed because the frozen inputs do not contain its exact selected cell table or binarization thresholds.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The contribution is the causal structural atlas, not generic two-copy quantifier elimination: rank-two segment orientations and the four exhaustive rank-one modes are glued through shared response endpoints, and design B is refined by the proved residual forest. Generic real-algebraic machinery is used only on each resulting one-copy target graph to enumerate components and compare their target projections. Legal boundary countermodels may contain zero mechanisms; strict positivity is asserted only for witnesses sampled from interior support charts. Agreement with Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki, Shingaki--Kuroki, and Kawakami is confined to their stated overlap domains. Known selection fixes population margins by normalization. The application conclusion remains conditional on the causal graph, proxy exclusion, instrument exogeneity and relevance, the imposed selection scheme, and the unavailable numerical GEUVADIS table.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem closes the single load-bearing mathematical gap by proving an exhaustive causal edge-state union before invoking any component algorithm.
statement_notes.gap: The new step is the simultaneous treatment of rank-one coincidences, inactive rows, split-coordinate faces, endpoint incidences, and IV residual forests without a two-copy classifier.
statement_notes.consumer: Every observable law in either finite design now receives an exact rigidity value or a legal target-changing SCM certificate.

statement_notes.justification: The cycle-to-SCM image equality and exhaustive atlas turn componentwise target projection into a necessary-and-sufficient full-SCM identification theorem.
statement_notes.gap: Existing proxy and NMF results do not characterize PN/PS constancy over every boundary component of this selected causal fiber.
statement_notes.consumer: Analysts obtain a definitive identifying map or an explicit observational-equivalence obstruction.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem verifies published regular formulas and proves that the same structural compiler remains defined on all singular and boundary fibers.
statement_notes.gap: The anchor paper does not supply a full-fiber classifier when its regular inversions fail.
statement_notes.consumer: Users can retain the published value on regular tables and switch to an exact rigidity or countermodel certificate elsewhere.

statement_notes.justification: The result derives exact target agreement on Kawakami's regular overlap and proves one selected singular law lies outside its loading-matrix domain.
statement_notes.gap: Kawakami's regular IV-plus-proxy theorem does not classify selected nonnegative response-cycle faces.
statement_notes.consumer: IV-plus-proxy users can distinguish overlap agreement from strict scope separation without a subsumption claim.

statement_notes.justification: Explicit mode counts and a cited one-copy real-algebraic bound yield finite termination, degree control, and rational-input certificate sizes.
statement_notes.gap: The complexity guarantee is for the causal structural compiler, not for an opaque raw-fiber two-copy test.
statement_notes.consumer: Exact-arithmetic implementations receive a checkable fixed-alphabet output envelope.

statement_notes.justification: Finite chart exhaustiveness, deterministic selection, common incident derivatives, and covariance separation make regular-stratum Wald inference operational.
statement_notes.gap: Published inverse-formula asymptotics do not cover rational and simple-algebraic charts selected from the complete atlas.
statement_notes.consumer: Separated rigid tables receive reproducible standard errors and ellipsoidal confidence regions, with an explicit fallback elsewhere.

statement_notes.justification: Exact preliminary coverage and discrete tail calibration prove finite-sample causal-target coverage without rank stability, while smooth separated charts recover Wald geometry.
statement_notes.gap: Changing identified sets require nuisance calibration over the complete SCM correspondence rather than empirical rank testing.
statement_notes.consumer: Boundary-sensitive PN/PS analyses receive honest uncertainty and do not mistake a nonshrinking confidence fiber for point identification.
